correctness.rationale: The normalized Fejér multiplier incl. |j−k|=n gives the exact form b*H_nb. The two endpoint columns cancel, so H_ne=0. Reflection commutes with H_n. On the symmetric subspace orthogonal to e the endpoints vanish, and the negative discrete Dirichlet Laplacian applied to H_n is 4/n times the identity there by the second difference of |j−k|. Its reflected symmetric modes are the odd-indexed Dirichlet modes, exactly the asserted symmetric cosines and reciprocal eigenvalues. On the antisymmetric subspace the sum is zero and (H_nv)_0−(H_nv)_1=4v₀/n, with the mirrored right endpoint relation. Thus the negative Neumann difference operator with replicated endpoint ghosts applied to H_n is 4/n times the identity there, including the n=1 boundary-only case. Its odd-indexed Neumann modes are precisely the listed antisymmetric centered sines. Each block has simple positive eigenvalues, and cross-block equality would require n to divide the odd symmetric numerator, which lies strictly between 0 and n. Comparing the largest available half-frequencies gives the even symmetric or odd antisymmetric minimum eigenvalue exactly. Orthogonal projection onto e gives the stated distance and equality only on the kernel plus the simple soft eigenspace, with nonzero soft direction attainable at any fixed angle. Zero Fejér deficit itself requires only the kernel.
residual_risks: The coefficient-space distance is for a chosen Fejér–Riesz factor, not an intrinsic function-space distance. Finite numerical checks do not replace the boundary and completeness arguments.
